topic: Malaysia: the Emergency, security policy, and anti-communist conflict
scope_decisions: The artifact set covers the 1948-1960 Malayan Emergency as the core event and treats post-1960 security practices as legacy rather than as a new primary topic.
The content stays focused on security policy, counterinsurgency, and anti-communist state formation instead of broad general Malaysian political history.
PDF-facing text uses English with limited controlled Malay and Simplified Chinese markers only.
The set avoids precise casualty totals, resettlement totals, and legal-code citations that would require more granular primary-source verification.
decisions: Use 18 June 1948 as the emergency declaration anchor and 31 July 1960 as the formal end date.
Treat the Briggs Plan, new villages, and Special Branch intelligence as the main counterinsurgency mechanisms.
Frame independence in 1957 as part of the political settlement that weakened the insurgency's colonial-war narrative.
Keep later anti-communist policy in the post-1960 section short so the artifact remains centered on the Emergency.
